beats.narration: Your seatbelt light won't turn off — even after you buckle up.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a car seat with a seatbelt buckled into its receptacle, static camera, warm interior daylight; quick cut to a dashboard instrument cluster with a seatbelt warning icon lit (generic icon, no readable brand text).
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two ~2s sub-shots (buckled belt, lit dashboard icon) before real generation.

beats.narration: The belt clicks in fine. The chime keeps going, or the icon stays lit anyway.

beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (latch click, persistent icon) before real generation.

beats.narration: That's usually the buckle switch — a small sensor inside the receptacle — not the belt itself.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro cutaway of a seatbelt buckle receptacle removed from its mount, interior mechanism visible, resting on a clean workbench, slow push-in on the small switch component inside.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (removed buckle, switch push-in) before real generation.

beats.narration: Wear, corrosion, or debris inside the buckle can stop it from registering a good latch.
beats.visualPrompt: Extreme macro on the buckle switch contact points showing light surface corrosion/dust, shallow depth of field; cut to a small precision tool resting beside the opened buckle housing on the workbench (tool at rest, not in use — no hand in frame).
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (corroded contacts, tool beside housing) before real generation.

beats.narration: Always wear the belt regardless — but a switch like that can point to a bigger electrical gremlin.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a buckled seatbelt across an empty seat, calm static hold, soft daylight — reinforcing 'always wear it' without showing a driver.

beats.narration: Worth checking it out. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.

adVariants.label: A_annoyance_first
adVariants.hook: That seatbelt chime that won't shut up? It's probably not the belt.
adVariants.caption: A worn or corroded buckle switch can keep the warning on even after you're buckled in tight. One clue: it's a sensor issue, not a safety failure — but it's worth a look.

evidence.note: General automotive-repair knowledge (the seatbelt warning light/chime is driven by a buckle switch inside the receptacle that detects whether the latch plate is seated; a worn, corroded, or debris-jammed switch can fail to register a properly buckled belt; this is a sensor/switch issue, not a webbing or pretensioner failure), not a shop-specific sourced fact.
